parsed.explanation: Travelers face a combined regime where national entry/document rules, government-funded facility exclusion, state criminal bans, and hostile custody converge. If outed, consequences include visa refusal or permanent inadmissibility, secondary screening, detention, criminal trespass, birth-sex facility placement, and documented immigration-custody sexual abuse/forced labor. Adult families add minor-care denial and possible out-of-state routing. Formal equality laws, hate-crime statutes, settlements, and court challenges exist, but none is documented as an operative traveler-facing shield against these restrictions. Public opinion and state threat framing raise social/police hostility. Absence of capital punishment keeps it above the worst tier, but universal facility and document exposure put it in high risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/visa rules treat sex as binary by birth, stop new nonbinary markers, refuse cases with document/appearance discrepancies, and allow permanent inadmissibility if misrepresentation is suspected. Reports say passports confiscated and travelers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing nonbinary markers remain valid until expiration; home-country passports may avoid domestic document processes. Courts and advocacy challenge policies, but no operative visitor protection is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: A border mismatch can trigger refusal, secondary screening, detention, and downstream facility or custody exposure; state document rules may reinforce doubt.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labor, beatings, solitary confinement, and sexual abuse. Corrections adopted conversion-style policies for trans inmates. First bathroom arrest included 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts may review detentions, and a national hate-crime statute exists, but no documented effective visitor release, consular, or custody-protection mechanism.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Fraud or document investigations can move into detention; a facility arrest can lead to birth-sex placement, and custody policies apply to outed travelers.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National orders bar transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. Many states ban schools and government buildings, some private settings, and four criminalize use under conditions. Documented trespass arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some mapped jurisdictions lack bans in these categories and some have anti-discrimination laws, but no visitor-facing facility protection is documented against national exclusion.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors in public buildings, schools, or transit may be excluded; refusal can become arrest under state law, operating inside the national regime.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care is banned in state/province and many jurisdictions; adult surgeries were cancelled after funding and legal pressure; insurance rules block youth reimbursement. Families may be denied care locally.
care_services.protection: A settlement pays dependents' medically necessary care under a public-employee plan, including minors treated outside the state/province; grandfathered minors may continue care.
care_services.interaction: A minor's care search can trigger document disclosure; national funding freezes and state bans combine to make care seeking risky or out-of-state.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders direct correction of trans workplace protections, rescind prison LGBTQ policy, and investigate schools. Reward and counterterrorism texts associate radical gender ideology with violent extremism. Polls show majority support for birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A national employment ruling and some state protections persist, and courts blocked or enjoined some orders, but no documented operative enforcement protects trans visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises police discretion and social confrontation; partial rule of law does not cancel facility, custody, entry, or document restrictions.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division documents fatal shootings and violent crimes against trans women; police called it epidemic-level, but without a background denominator the rate remains uncertain. If attacked, custody and facility systems may re-victimize.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A national hate-crime statute and some police investigations exist; 22 state/provinces protect against gender-identity discrimination, but visitor reporting and remedy effectiveness are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street friction may escalate at facility, border, or service checks; police response may be shaped by document mismatch and official hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care bans and school or social-transition criminalization threaten traveling families; guardians may face denied care, out-of-state routing, and inquiry risk; children can be excluded or mismatched at facility and document checks.
minors_guardians.protection: Settlement coverage may fund minor dependents' care, grandfathered HRT continues, and guardianship may aid some state services; no traveler-facing protection is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult plus minor increases document scrutiny; care denial can turn a medical trip into investigation or outing, while national and state rules interact.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Legal challenges are unresolved; some bans or orders are blocked, modified, or pending; foreign advisories show uncertainty; visitor outcomes for fraud waivers, consular access, and custody remedies are thin.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, ombuds processes, advocacy FAQs, and appeals sometimes provide relief, but none is documented as a reliable traveler-facing remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Exposure varies by jurisdiction and moment; a traveler cannot predict whether national, state, or court authority will control the encounter.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A describes routine visitor arrests, months in pretrial with beatings, and an execution threat. This jurisdiction lacks routine arrest for presentation and credible capital penalty, but has entry fraud/refusal and severe immigration custody, so it sits above 0.15-A.

0.25-C has birth-sex prison placement, cross-dressing arrest, and slow courts. This jurisdiction is similar but slightly lower: national visa screening, facility bans, and documented immigration-custody abuse broaden traveler exposure beyond the anchor's local custody harm.

0.35-A is border exclusion and humiliation without credible custody or execution. Here discovery can bring refusal or fraud bars, facility denial, trespass arrest, birth-sex custody, and reported sexual abuse in immigration detention, so it rates materially below 0.35-A.

0.75-C offers trained border officers, release with recourse, and low to moderate detention harm. This combined regime has binary documents, government facility exclusion, hostile custody practices, and contested protections, so it is far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: National binary document policy and visa discrepancy screening can trigger investigation; a mismatch or refusal then flows into facility and custody exposure. Government facility bans and some state criminal trespass laws force either compliant use or refusal-to-depart arrest. Once in custody, conversion-style or birth-sex placement harms appear. For families, minor-care prohibitions and funding freezes turn care seeking into possible denial, disclosure, or interstate movement. Partial protections and litigation are unstable; traveler remedies are thin. Thus the operative regime's severity dominates: high risk without the credible execution or imprisonment of the lowest tier.
